sources.researchNote: The Commons file dates the photograph 15 January 1936. The scene, with summer clothing, foliage and an open-air crowd, does not suit mid-January, so that date may record cataloguing rather than the day the photograph was taken; the year is kept as uncertain.

media.title: Jan Kiepura singing on Plac Piłsudskiego, Warsaw, 1936 — photograph by Henryk Poddębski
media.description: Jan Kiepura singing from a balcony to a crowd on Plac Piłsudskiego in Warsaw, photographed by Henryk Poddębski. Kiepura, the star of Ein Lied für Dich and Tout pour l’amour, kept the Kaper–Jurmann songs before European audiences after the composers left for America.
media.altText: Black-and-white photograph of Jan Kiepura singing from a decorated balcony above a large open-air crowd, with long banners hanging from the colonnade.
media.publicCaption: Jan Kiepura singing to a crowd on Plac Piłsudskiego, Warsaw, 1936. Photograph by Henryk Poddębski.
media.publicCreditLine: Henryk Poddębski; Biblioteka Narodowa / Polona; via Wikimedia Commons.
media.rightsNote: Public domain. Henryk Poddębski died in 1945, so the Polish term of life and seventy years ran out at the end of 2015. In the United States the photograph is free either way: published in Poland without a reservation of copyright, it was never protected there and the URAA restored nothing; if unpublished, its term of life and seventy years ran out with the Polish one. The local copy is reduced to 2000 px.

timelineEvents.title: European afterlife
timelineEvents.label: 1934–1936 · European afterlife
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Jurmann–Kaper films and songs continued circulating in Europe as the composers left for America.
timelineEvents.longDescription: The composers’ European films and songs continued to circulate as they left for America. In September 1934, Madame wird kinderlieb played in Stuttgart with Jurmann and Kaper credited, despite Nazi purges. In France, Tout pour l’amour with Kiepura screened as late as 1936; the Journal de Vichy called their music “infiniment plaisante”.
